imp.generic: I arrived at the house and was relieved to find it pleasant.
imp.author: I suppose I had expected, or had dreaded, something so melancholy that what greeted me was a good surprise; and as we turned into the avenue I encountered a reprieve that was probably but a proof of the point to which my fortitude had sunk.

imp.generic: The housekeeper was glad to see me, which made me a little suspicious.
imp.author: I perceived within half an hour that she was so glad—stout, simple, plain, clean, wholesome woman—as to be positively on her guard against showing it too much; and I wondered even then, a little, why she should wish not to show it.

imp.generic: The children were unusually well-behaved, and it unsettled me.
imp.author: Their magnificent little surrender belonged, I mean, just to the special array of the facts that were most abysmal; for why, after all, did they never resent my inexorable, my perpetual society?

imp.generic: I thought the child was lying to me.
imp.author: At that moment, in the state of my nerves, I absolutely believed she lied; and if I once more closed my eyes it was before the dazzle of the three or four possible ways in which I might take this up.

imp.generic: Autumn came and the place looked bleak.
imp.author: The summer had turned, the summer had gone; the autumn had dropped upon Bly and had blown out half our lights, so that the place, with its gray sky and withered garlands, was like a theater after the performance—all strewn with crumpled playbills.

imp.generic: I was afraid to say the names out loud.
imp.author: I always broke down in the monstrous utterance of names; as they died away on my lips I said to myself that I should indeed help them to represent something infamous if, by pronouncing them, I should violate as rare a little case of instinctive delicacy as any schoolroom had ever known.

imp.generic: He admitted he took the letter, and I was overjoyed.
imp.author: Out of his white little face there presently came a sound, not low nor weak, but as if from much further away, that I drank like a waft of fragrance—'Yes—I took it'—and at this, with a moan of joy, I enfolded, I drew him close.

imp.generic: Maybe the boy was innocent after all, which terrified me.
imp.author: Within a minute there had come to me, out of my very pity, the appalling alarm of his being perhaps innocent; it was for the instant confounding and bottomless, for if he were innocent, what then, on earth, was I?

imp.generic: I realized I was the only one who could see the danger clearly.
imp.author: My lucidity must have seemed awful; but it has only made me, I now so strangely see, more lucid—made me get hold of still other things, things that have delighted, fascinated, and yet, at bottom, mystified and troubled me.

imp.generic: Then the boy died in my arms.
imp.author: I caught him, yes, I held him—it may be imagined with what a passion; but at the end of a minute I began to feel what it truly was that I held: we were alone with the quiet day, and his little heart, dispossessed, had stopped.
